issue.title: gateway: TestBusy red under load (after the stream, Last is set but nothing counted)
issue.body:
`TestBusy` (internal/gateway) went red in a full `go test ./... -timeout 45m` on mote (macOS 27, load 60 to 250 from several sessions' suites) at 10-28 23:56, at origin/main e15b2277c plus a Library-only change that internal/gateway doesn't import for this test:

```
--- FAIL: TestBusy (4.04s)
    busy_test.go:70: after the stream: {Requests:0 Tools:0 Last:2026-10-28 23:56:47.65966 -0700 PDT Bridge:0 BridgeLast:0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC}
```

The same package then timed out at 45m (#2870, #4228). Not rerun alone; the cause isn't found. Not taking it.

comments.body:
A test-only fix is on [fix/4235-busy-test-handler-completion](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/4235-busy-test-handler-completion), commit [6c1cc813](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/6c1cc813ac37ab962595f7055a8bacd5913a3e6a), based on upstream `ed0ab567`.

The test now waits for the real gateway POST handler to return before checking the request counts, and checks that `Last` falls between request start and handler completion. It no longer assumes the test will inspect `Last` within five seconds. The held HTTP stream and tool-accounting checks remain. Production code is unchanged.

The unchanged test passed here, so the original load-dependent failure was not reproduced directly. A controlled overlay modeling a six-second late observation makes the old elapsed-time assertion fail with zero active requests; a separate mutation removing request accounting is still caught by the updated test. The related gateway tests pass under `-race`, as do package vet/build and formatting checks. I independently reran the related race tests.

This addresses the demonstrated timing assumption; it does not establish that it was the sole cause of the original report. The full suite was not run. AI-assisted implementation and review.
